drills.title: What does this print?
drills.promptMd: Trace each call to `count()` carefully — decide what the static local holds before you settle on an answer.
drills.explanationMd: `s_calls` is a **static local**: it is initialized once (to `0`) on the very first call, then survives between calls instead of being destroyed when `count()` returns. Each call increments it and prints the new value, so the output climbs `1 → 2 → 3`. The common trap is expecting `1 1 1` (as if the initializer ran every time — it doesn't) or `0 1 2` (as if the value was printed before the increment rather than after).

drills.title: Shadow and scope resolution
drills.promptMd: A local variable shares its name with a global. Trace each output statement and commit to an answer.
drills.explanationMd: Inside `show()`, the local `g_score { 99 }` shadows the global. An unqualified `g_score` (line A) refers to the nearest enclosing declaration — the local — so it prints `99`. The leading `::` on line B explicitly requests the **global namespace**, bypassing the shadow entirely, so it prints the global value `10`. The shadow never touches the global object; they are two completely separate variables.

drills.title: Off-by-one in the ID dispenser
drills.promptMd: This ID dispenser should hand out `0` on the first call, `1` on the second, and so on — but it hands out `1, 2, 3` instead. Fix it.
drills.explanationMd: Pre-increment (`++s_id`) increments the variable *before* returning it, so the first call yields `1` — not `0`. Post-increment (`s_id++`) returns the *current* value and then advances the stored counter, so the first call yields `0`, the second `1`, and so on. The chapter lab's `nextCounterId()` uses this same post-increment idiom to hand out IDs starting from a base value.

drills.title: Shadow in the branch discards the result
drills.promptMd: `classify()` always returns `"unknown"` no matter what you pass in. Find the shadow that is burying each branch's result and remove it.
drills.explanationMd: Each `if` branch was declaring a *new* `std::string_view label` inside its own block. That inner variable shadows the outer `label`, is assigned the correct string, and then immediately destroyed when the block closes — the outer `label` is never touched and stays `"unknown"`. The fix is to assign to the existing outer `label` rather than declaring a fresh one in each branch.

drills.title: Implement a unique-event-ID dispenser
drills.promptMd: Write `nextEventId()` so that each call returns the next integer in sequence, starting at `100` on the first call. Use a static local variable — no global state.
drills.explanationMd: Declare `static int s_nextId { 100 };` — the `static` keyword gives the local **static duration**, so `s_nextId` is initialized once (to `100`) on the very first call and persists for the program's lifetime. Use post-increment (`s_nextId++`) so the current value is returned *before* the counter advances: first call yields `100`, second `101`, and so on. A global counter would do the same job, but a static local seals the state inside the function — only `nextEventId()` can access it.
